newsitem.title: IRAN: "Tehran vampire" killer hanged from crane.
newsitem.headline: "Tehran vampire" killer hanged from crane.

text.p: An Iranian serial killer dubbed "Tehran Vampire" was hanged from a mobile crane in Tehran on Wednesday as a crowd of some 20,000 people looked on.
The crowd had gathered by dawn at the Olympic Village district in west Tehran to see 28-year-old Gholamreza Khoshrou Kouran Kordieh lashed by his victims' male relatives before his public execution.
Khoshrou was condemned to 10 death sentences this month after confessing on television to the kidnap, rape and murder of nine girls and women aged 10 to 47 in four months this year.
The tenth death sentence was for rape in 1993.
Khoshrou carried out his crimes by night posing as a freelance taxi driver in the streets close to the site of his hanging, earning himself the title of the Tehran vampire.

"Innocent blood will always be avenged...This is punishment for the criminal but for us witnesses it is a lesson to be learned...We are responsible for our actions," a robed cleric told the crowd before the sentence was carried out.
Verses from the Koran, were relayed through loudspeakers to onlookers who had fought through three km (two miles) traffic jams to get to the scene.

The crowd, kept away from the crane by a line of police armed with wooden batons stationed on top of a surrounding low brick wall, surged to the wall when Khoshrou was brought in front of them with his hands tied.
Officials threw Khoshrou down on his stomach onto a low bench where he was then given 214 lashes by male relatives of the victims in a period of just under 10 minutes.

Members of the crowd, some perched up on trees and road signs for better vantage points, counted out the number of lashes and cheered the relatives most of whom had been restrained by officials from carrying out more attacks on the prostrate Khoshrou.
Khoshrou, who was not blind-folded, alternatively turned his head towards the crowd and those carrying out the lashing.
He was then led a short distance to the crane where a rope was placed around his neck before being slowly winched some 100 metres off the ground.
"It's a sweet death for him. He deserves worse," said Maryam Bakhti who believes she was very nearly one of Khoshrou victims.
Bakhti, a 29-year-old graduate, said she got into Khoshrou's car one evening in 1994 and had to fight her way out of the car after he drove down a dark side street.
She now carries a knife in her handbag.
"When I saw him on the television I just shivered...The police were very slow in telling us there was a murderer among us," she told Reuters.
Newspapers have reported that Khoshrou burned his victims so that they could not be identified.
Relatives of the murdered victims had called for Khoshrou to be stoned to death. They had also called for his hands to be cut off before execution because he had also been accused of theft.
